wp: WP1 Identity, config and run modes (plus state.json write discipline)
summary: Adds src/config.ts (one Config object, INSTA_OSS_* env, read once in main.ts, injected into buildServer), a 'local' | 'server' run mode sharing one code path, and server-mode identity: first-visit admin creation through the cloud's Better Auth mount path POST /api/auth/sign-up/email (refused once an admin exists), sign-in / get-session / sign-out on the same mount, the cloud's /auth/login, /auth/refresh, /auth/logout wrappers for `insta login --email`, the cloud's GET/POST/DELETE /tokens minting `insta_` keys (insta_ + 64 [a-zA-Z], sha256-stored, same ApiToken record shape), /me returning the admin as the cloud's PublicUser with `via`, and a bearer-or-signed-cookie guard on every route except /healthz, /api/auth/*, /auth/* and the SPA shell. Passwords use node:crypto scrypt; sessions are 32-char tokens stored hashed with Better Auth's 7-day expiry, 1-day sliding update and the exact `better-auth.session_token` signed-cookie format. Local mode is byte-for-byte today's behaviour (127.0.0.1, no guard, `/me` = local, /tokens 501). state.ts gains an atomic tmp+rename write, a sync-only assertion for mutate(), a heartbeat lock file so two daemons never share one data dir, and a coalesced touch buffer so token lastUsedAt never causes a per-request rewrite; activity stamps are declared out of state.json entirely. No dependency added.

files.change: NEW. `export type RunMode = 'local' | 'server'`; `export interface Config` (fields in sharedSurface.config); `export function loadConfig(env = process.env, argv = process.argv): Config` (pure, throws on invalid values, no I/O except reading/creating <dataDir>/secret in server mode when INSTA_OSS_SECRET is unset); `export function isDaemonHost(cfg, host): 'api' | 'console' | null`; `export function publicUrl(cfg, kind: 'api'|'console'): string`. Replaces the ad-hoc reads in src/main.ts:12-13 (INSTA_OSS_PORT / --port), src/state.ts:17 (INSTA_OSS_STATE), src/adapters/garage.ts:25 (INSTA_OSS_GARAGE_CONFIG), src/adapters/garage.ts:202,210 (INSTA_OSS_S3_HOST_ENDPOINT), src/server.ts:671 (INSTA_OSS_UI_DIST).

NEW, pure (no fastify, no fs): scrypt hash/verify with constant-time compare and a fixed dummy hash for unknown-email timing parity; session mint/verify/slide/revoke; insta_ token mint/verify/revoke/list; signed-cookie encode/decode in Better Auth's format; PublicUser/ApiToken/Session output mappers; in-memory per-IP failure limiter for sign-in. Operates on the `identity` slot of State through the state.ts helpers.

NEW: `registerAuth(app: FastifyInstance, cfg: Config)`: the onRequest guard hook (server mode only), the /api/auth/{sign-up/email,sign-in/email,get-session,sign-out} routes, the /auth/{login,refresh,logout} routes, /me, /tokens GET/POST/DELETE, plus the `/auth/signup` 501. In local mode it registers only today's /me (server.ts:55) and today's /tokens 501s (server.ts:58-60), so local behaviour is unchanged. Decorates `req.actor: { userId, via: 'jwt' | 'api', scopes? }` like the cloud's Actor (insta-platform src/auth/service.ts:26).

`buildServer(engine: Engine, cfg: Config = loadConfig())` (tests keep calling with one argument, test/server.test.ts:88). `Fastify({ logger: false, trustProxy: cfg.trustProxy })`. Delete the inline /me (line 55) and /tokens 501s (lines 58-60); call `registerAuth(app, cfg)` right after the content-type parser (line 33) so the hook precedes every route. `isApiPath` (line 672-673) gains '/api' and '/auth'. `uiDist` (line 671) comes from cfg.uiDist. SPA shell: register fastifyStatic with `index: false`; a `shell(reply)` helper reads index.html once (cached) and injects `<script>window.__INSTA_OSS__=${JSON.stringify({mode, setupRequired, consoleUrl, apiUrl})}</script>` before `</head>`; `GET /` and the not-found fallback (lines 676-678) send the shell. `setupRequired` is recomputed per request (cheap: identity.admin presence).

`const cfg = loadConfig()`; `initStatePath(cfg.statePath)`; `acquireLock(cfg.dataDir)` before the Docker check (line 16); construct adapters with cfg (garage config path / S3 host endpoint via constructor options, not env); `app.listen({ host: cfg.listenHost, port: cfg.port })` (replaces the hard-coded '127.0.0.1' at line 21); banner: local = today's three lines (22-24); server = `api ${cfg.apiUrl}`, `console ${cfg.consoleUrl}`, and while no admin exists `setup: ${cfg.consoleUrl}/setup`. SIGTERM/SIGINT: release the lock, close the server.

NEW, fake adapters (copy the adapter fakes from test/server.test.ts into test/fakes.ts and import from both), `buildServer(engine, loadConfig({ INSTA_OSS_MODE: 'server', INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN: 'example.test', INSTA_OSS_SECRET: 's'.repeat(32), INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR: tmp, INSTA_OSS_STATE: tmp/state.json }))`: (1) 401 sweep over every registered route (`app.printRoutes` / hasRoute) except the allowlist, asserting `{error:'unauthorized'}` and `www-authenticate`; (2) sign-up creates the admin, returns `{token,user}` + Set-Cookie, second sign-up 422; (3) sign-in wrong password 401 `{code:'INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD'}`, right password 200 `{redirect:false, token, user}`; (4) get-session with cookie / with bearer / with nothing (`null`); sign-out clears cookie and invalidates the token; (5) /me shapes `{user: PublicUser, via:'jwt'}` and `via:'api'` with an insta_ key; (6) /tokens create (201 `{token, record}`), list (newest first, revoked rows carry revokedAt), delete (200 `{ok:true}`, second delete 404), expired token 401, revoked token 401, `orgId:'x'` 400; (7) /auth/login → AuthResult with accessToken === refreshToken, /auth/refresh with a session token → AuthResult, with an insta_ key → 401, /auth/logout → `{ok:true}` always; (8) Origin mismatch on a cookie-authenticated POST → 403, same Origin passes, bearer requests ignore Origin; (9) `GET /` shell contains `__INSTA_OSS__` with setupRequired true then false; (10) after `--reset-admin` (call the exported `resetAdmin()`), sign-up works again and old tokens still verify.

Keeps passing unchanged (local mode default). ADD: `loadConfig({})` defaults test (mode local, listenHost 127.0.0.1, port 8080, dataDir ~/.insta-oss, domain localhost, auth disabled); `loadConfig({INSTA_OSS_MODE:'server'})` without INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN throws; `--port 9999` argv wins over default and INSTA_OSS_PORT wins over argv (today's precedence at main.ts:13); local `/me` is exactly `{user:{id:'local',email:null,name:'local'}}` (no `via`); local /tokens still 501 (already asserted at lines 207-208, 224).

NEW, no Docker: mutate() rejects an async callback; saveState leaves no partial file (tmp is renamed); acquireLock twice in one process throws; a lock with a stale heartbeat (mtime > 60 s old) is taken over; a fresh heartbeat refuses with the holder's pid in the message; touchLater flushes on releaseLock.

ADD: `me()` GET /me; `session()` GET /api/auth/get-session; `signUp(name,email,password)` POST /api/auth/sign-up/email; `signIn(email,password)` POST /api/auth/sign-in/email; `signOut()` POST /api/auth/sign-out; `tokens()`, `createToken(name, expiresInDays?)`, `revokeToken(id)`. `call()` gains `credentials:'same-origin'` (explicit) and, on 401 when `window.__INSTA_OSS__?.mode === 'server'`, dispatches a `insta-oss:unauthenticated` event the router listens to.

Routes `/setup` (Setup page: name, email, password ×2, then a 'Create a CLI token' step showing `insta login --api-key <k> --api-url <apiUrl>`), `/login`, `/tokens`. Gate: in server mode, `Home` first calls `api.session()`; null + `__INSTA_OSS__.setupRequired` → `/setup`; null otherwise → `/login`; the `insta-oss:unauthenticated` event navigates to `/login`. Local mode: no gate, today's flow. Layout gets a sign-out item and a Tokens nav entry (server mode only).

sharedSurface.engineSeams: None required inside src/engine.ts for this WP; the Engine constructor and every method keep their signatures. Seams this WP creates for other WPs: (1) `buildServer(engine, cfg)` and `registerAuth(app, cfg)`: the router WP's HTTP lane forwards api.<domain> / console.<domain> to this listener and must forward `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `Host` unchanged (cookieSecure and req.ip depend on them under trustProxy). (2) `isDaemonHost(cfg, host)` in config.ts is the single rule for which hostnames belong to the daemon itself (api., console., plus '127.0.0.1'/'localhost'/'[::1]' with or without port in local mode); the router calls it before consulting the service hostname map. (3) `req.actor` is available to the router's in-process wake path only if it goes through the API (it does not; lanes are unauthenticated by design, like the cloud proxy). (4) state.ts: scheduler and router MUST keep activity stamps in memory (a Map keyed by `${branchRef}:${serviceKind}:${name}`), never in state.json; `touchLater` exists only for low-rate audit fields (token lastUsedAt, session updatedAt). (5) `initStatePath` must be called before the first `loadState()`; main.ts does it; tests that set INSTA_OSS_STATE keep working through the env fallback. (6) `acquireLock(dataDir)` must be the first thing main.ts does after loadConfig; integration tests that spawn a daemon must pass a distinct INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR. (7) The scheduler WP's 'explicit start' and 'deploy' wake doors read `desiredState` from state as today (engine.ts:578) and are unaffected. (8) Template/project WPs that add routes register them AFTER registerAuth so the guard covers them automatically; any new public route must be added to the allowlist in auth.ts explicitly (there is no other way to bypass the hook).

algorithm:
## 0. Vocabulary
- `now()` = injectable clock (Date.now) so identity.ts tests are deterministic.
- `b64url(buf)` = Buffer.toString('base64url'); `b64(buf)` = standard base64 (cookie signature only, to match better-call).
- `sha256hex(s)` = createHash('sha256').update(s,'utf8').digest('hex').
- `randomAlpha(n, alphabet)`: draw bytes with randomBytes in batches, keep b when b < 256 - (256 % alphabet.length) (rejection sampling, unbiased), map to alphabet[b % len].
- `SESSION_ALPHABET` = a-zA-Z0-9 (Better Auth generateId, @better-auth/core dist/utils/id.mjs:3-5); `KEY_ALPHABET` = a-zA-Z (api-key plugin defaultKeyGenerator, dist/index.mjs:2294-2296).

## 1. loadConfig(env, argv)
1. mode = env.INSTA_OSS_MODE ?? 'local'; if not 'local'|'server' throw Error(`INSTA_OSS_MODE must be local or server`).
2. port: if env.INSTA_OSS_PORT defined use Number(it); else if argv contains '--port' use Number(next); else 8080. Same precedence as src/main.ts:12-13. Reject NaN / out of 1..65535.
3. dataDir = env.INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR ?? (mode === 'server' ? '/var/lib/instacloud' : join(homedir(), '.insta-oss')); must be absolute (path.isAbsolute) else throw. Do NOT mkdir here (main.ts does `mkdirSync(dataDir, {recursive:true})` after loadConfig; loadConfig stays pure except step 9).
4. statePath = env.INSTA_OSS_STATE ?? join(dataDir, 'state.json'); garageConfigPath = env.INSTA_OSS_GARAGE_CONFIG ?? join(dataDir, 'garage.toml'); s3HostEndpoint = env.INSTA_OSS_S3_HOST_ENDPOINT ?? 'http://127.0.0.1:3900'; uiDist = env.INSTA_OSS_UI_DIST ?? join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', 'ui', 'dist').
5. domain: server → env.INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN required (throw `INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN is required in server mode (the installer sets it; e.g. 203-0-113-7.sslip.io)`); local → env.INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN ?? 'localhost'. Lowercase, trim trailing dot, validate /^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)*$/.
6. listenHost = env.INSTA_OSS_LISTEN_HOST ?? (server ? '0.0.0.0' : '127.0.0.1').
7. apiUrl = env.INSTA_OSS_API_URL ?? (server ? `https://api.${domain}` : `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`); consoleUrl = env.INSTA_OSS_CONSOLE_URL ?? (server ? `https://console.${domain}` : apiUrl). Both parsed with `new URL` (throw on failure), trailing slash stripped.
8. trustProxy = bool(env.INSTA_OSS_TRUST_PROXY, default server); auth.enabled = bool(env.INSTA_OSS_AUTH, default server). bool(): '1'|'true' → true, '0'|'false' → false, else throw.
9. auth.secret (only when auth.enabled): env.INSTA_OSS_SECRET; if absent: p = join(dataDir,'secret'); if exists read+trim; else mkdirSync(dataDir,{recursive:true}); writeFileSync(p, randomBytes(32).toString('hex'), {mode:0o600}); read it. Throw if length < 32. (This is the one side effect; documented in the file header.)
10. auth.sessionTtlSec = int(env.INSTA_OSS_SESSION_TTL_SEC, 604800, min 60); sessionUpdateAgeSec = 86400; cookieSecure = consoleUrl.startsWith('https://'); cookieName = (cookieSecure ? '__Secure-' : '') + 'better-auth.session_token'.
11. router.* and sleep.* per the config table; int() helper validates finite integers within [min,max].
12. Return Object.freeze(cfg).
13. `isDaemonHost(cfg, hostHeader)`: strip port (`host.replace(/:\d+$/,'')`, IPv6 literal handled with a bracket check), lowercase; return 'api' if === `api.${domain}` or (local mode and host ∈ {'127.0.0.1','localhost','[::1]','::1'}); 'console' if === `console.${domain}`; else null. In local mode the loopback names count as BOTH api and console ('api' is returned, and buildServer treats api|console alike for static serving in local mode).

## 2. Boot (main.ts)
1. cfg = loadConfig(); handle `--reset-admin` (section 9) before anything else.
2. mkdirSync(cfg.dataDir,{recursive:true}); initStatePath(cfg.statePath); acquireLock(cfg.dataDir) (section 8).
3. Docker check as today (main.ts:16-17).
4. engine = new Engine(new LocalPostgres(), new DockerCompute(), new LocalGarage({configPath: cfg.garageConfigPath, hostEndpoint: cfg.s3HostEndpoint}), new LocalManagedDb()).
5. app = buildServer(engine, cfg); await app.listen({host: cfg.listenHost, port: cfg.port}).
6. Banner: local → today's lines verbatim (main.ts:22-24). server → `insta-oss daemon (server mode) api ${cfg.apiUrl}  console ${cfg.consoleUrl}`; if loadState().identity?.admin is null → `setup: ${cfg.consoleUrl}/setup  (create the admin there, then mint a CLI token)`.
7. process.on('SIGTERM'|'SIGINT') → app.close() then releaseLock() then exit(0).

## 3. Identity primitives (identity.ts)
### 3.1 Passwords
- `hashPassword(pw)`: salt = randomBytes(16); key = scryptSync(pw.normalize('NFKC'), salt, 64, {N: 16384, r: 8, p: 1, maxmem: 64*1024*1024}); return `scrypt$16384$8$1$${b64url(salt)}$${b64url(key)}`.
- `verifyPassword(pw, stored)`: parse the 6 fields; recompute with the stored N,r,p (forward-compatible cost changes); return timingSafeEqual(key, storedKey) (lengths equal by construction; if lengths differ return false without throwing).
- `DUMMY_HASH` = hashPassword('insta-oss-dummy') computed once at module load; sign-in for an unknown email runs verifyPassword against DUMMY_HASH so timing does not reveal whether the admin email matched (mirrors Better Auth sign-in.mjs:210-212).
- Password policy: length >= 8 (Better Auth minPasswordLength 8, betterauth.ts:246), <= 256; else 400 {code:'PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT', message:'Password too short'} / {code:'PASSWORD_TOO_LONG', message:'Password too long'}.
- Email: trim + lowercase (cloud normalizeEmail, policy.ts:5); must match /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ else 400 {code:'INVALID_EMAIL', message:'Invalid email'}.

### 3.2 Admin creation (sign-up)
Inside one mutate():
1. s.identity ??= EMPTY_IDENTITY clone. If s.identity.admin !== null → throw AdminExists.
2. id = existingAdminId ?? randomAlpha(32, SESSION_ALPHABET) (existingAdminId is kept across `--reset-admin`, stored as s.identity.adminIdSeed; simpler: `--reset-admin` sets admin to null but leaves `s.identity.previousAdminId`, and sign-up reuses it so tokens keep their userId).
3. admin = {id, email, name: name?.trim() || email.split('@')[0], passwordHash, createdAt: iso, updatedAt: iso}.
4. Mint a session (3.3) in the same mutate (autoSignIn, sign-up.mjs:252-263). Return {admin, token}.
HTTP: 200 {token, user: betterAuthUser(admin)} + Set-Cookie (3.5). AdminExists → 422 {code:'USER_ALREADY_EXISTS', message:'an admin already exists on this daemon; sign in instead'}.

### 3.3 Sessions
- `mintSession(s, userId, ip, ua, rememberMe=true)`: token = randomAlpha(32, SESSION_ALPHABET); row = {id: randomUUID(), tokenHash: sha256hex(token), userId, createdAt: t, updatedAt: t, expiresAt: t + (rememberMe ? sessionTtlSec : 86400)s, ipAddress: ip, userAgent: ua}; push; return {token, row}. (rememberMe=false → 24 h, internal-adapter.mjs:180.)
- `findSession(s, token)`: h = sha256hex(token); row = sessions.find(r => r.tokenHash === h); if !row → null; if expiresAt <= now → delete row via touchLater, return null; if now - updatedAt >= sessionUpdateAgeSec*1000 → touchLater(r.updatedAt = now, r.expiresAt = now + sessionTtlSec) (Better Auth sliding update, updateAge 1 d); return row.
- `revokeSession(s, token)`: remove by hash. `revokeAllSessions(s)`: sessions = [].
- GC: on every mintSession, drop rows with expiresAt <= now.
- Session lookup is O(n) over a list that holds at most the admin's live sessions; fine.

### 3.4 insta_ tokens
- `mintToken(s, {name, scopes, expiresInDays})`: validate name (trim, 1..100 chars, else 400 'name is required' / 'name too long'); expiresInDays undefined|null → expiresAt null; else must be integer 1..3650 else 400. key = 'insta_' + randomAlpha(64, KEY_ALPHABET) (70 chars total, same as the cloud's plugin output). row = {id: randomUUID(), name, prefix:'insta_', keyHash: sha256hex(key), orgId: null, scopes: scopes ?? [], lastUsedAt: null, expiresAt, revokedAt: null, createdAt}. unshift so newest first. Return {token: key, record: apiTokenOut(row)}.
- `verifyToken(s, key)`: if key.length !== 70 || !/^insta_[A-Za-z]{64}$/.test(key) → null (cheap reject, mirrors the plugin's length check dist/index.mjs:2334); h = sha256hex(key); row = tokens.find(r => r.keyHash === h); null if !row || row.revokedAt || (row.expiresAt && row.expiresAt <= now). On success touchLater(r.lastUsedAt = now) (coalesced, never a synchronous state write on the request path). Return {userId: admin.id, via:'api', scopes: row.scopes}.
- `revokeToken(s, id)`: row with id and revokedAt null → revokedAt = now, return true; else false → 404 'token not found'.
- Scopes are recorded and echoed but not enforced: the single admin owns everything (documented in COMPATIBILITY.md; the cloud enforces scopes per org role, out of scope here).

### 3.5 Cookie (Better Auth wire format, so a Better Auth client works unchanged)
- name = cfg.auth.cookieName.
- value = encodeURIComponent(`${token}.${b64(hmacSha256(secret, token))}`) (better-call dist/crypto.mjs:22-31: HMAC-SHA256 over the raw token, standard base64, then URL-encoded).
- attributes: `Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=${sessionTtlSec}` (+ `; Secure` when cookieSecure). rememberMe=false → no Max-Age (session cookie), matching setSessionCookie (cookies/index.mjs:118-127).
- parse: split the Cookie header on ';', trim, find name (accept the `__Secure-` form and the bare form, as getSessionCookie does, cookies/index.mjs:210-215), decodeURIComponent, split at the LAST '.', recompute the HMAC and timingSafeEqual (compare Buffers of equal length; if lengths differ → invalid). Invalid signature → treated as absent.
- clear: same name with `Max-Age=0` and an empty value.

### 3.6 Sign-in rate limiter (server mode, in memory)
Map<ip, {failures: number[]}>: on failure push now, drop entries older than 15 min; if length >= 10 before the attempt → 429 {code:'TOO_MANY_REQUESTS', message:'too many sign-in attempts; try again later'} without running scrypt; on success delete the ip. ip = req.ip (fastify honours X-Forwarded-For under trustProxy). Also applies to /auth/login (same bucket). Not persisted; a restart resets it (acceptable: scrypt itself costs ~50 ms per guess).

## 4. Request guard (auth.ts, server mode only)
`app.addHook('onRequest', guard)`; runs before routing for every request:
1. path = req.url.split('?')[0].
2. Public if: path === '/healthz'; path.startsWith('/api/auth/'); path.startsWith('/auth/'); or (req.method === 'GET' && !isApiPath(path)) i.e. static assets and the SPA shell (the setup page must load without a session). isApiPath is the server.ts list plus '/api' and '/auth', so `/api/auth/anything-unknown` still 404s as JSON rather than serving the shell.
3. Otherwise resolve the actor (4.1); on null → reply 401 {error:'unauthorized'} with header `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="insta-oss"` (cloud sends `{error:'unauthorized'}` for every UnauthorizedError, server.ts:174-178; we omit the resource_metadata hint because we serve no protected-resource metadata).
4. CSRF belt for cookie-authenticated state changes: if actor.source === 'cookie' and method ∉ {GET, HEAD, OPTIONS}: require the `Origin` header (or, if absent, `Sec-Fetch-Site` ∈ {same-origin, none}) to have host === req.headers.host; else 403 {error:'cross-site request rejected'}. Bearer requests skip this (a bearer cannot be attached by a cross-site form). SameSite=Lax already blocks cross-site POST cookies; this is defence in depth.
5. Attach req.actor = {userId, via, scopes}.
### 4.1 Actor resolution (shared by the guard, /me, get-session, /auth/refresh)
a. h = req.headers.authorization; if h?.startsWith('Bearer '): t = h.slice(7).trim(); if t === '' → null; if t.startsWith('insta_') → verifyToken (3.4) or null (an insta_ key that fails must NOT fall through to session lookup, service.ts:57-59); else findSession(t) → {userId, via:'jwt', source:'bearer'} or null.
b. No bearer → cookie (3.5): valid signature → findSession(token) → {…, via:'jwt', source:'cookie'}; else null.
c. Any actor requires identity.admin !== null and admin.id === userId; otherwise null (covers `--reset-admin`: old sessions die, tokens keep working once the admin is recreated with the same id).
Order matters: bearer wins over cookie (Better Auth's bearer plugin converts Authorization to the session cookie, dist/plugins/bearer/index.mjs:25-28).

## 5. Route handlers (server mode)
- POST /api/auth/sign-up/email: body {name?, email, password}; validate (3.1) → 400 with Better Auth codes; run 3.2; Set-Cookie; 200 {token, user}. The route stays registered after setup so the response is the same 422 the cloud's mount gives for a duplicate user, instead of a 404 the SPA would mis-read.
- POST /api/auth/sign-in/email: limiter check; admin null → 401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD after verifyPassword(pw, DUMMY_HASH) (no setup hint on a public route); email mismatch → dummy verify → 401; verifyPassword false → record failure → 401; success → clear failures, mintSession(rememberMe), Set-Cookie, header `set-auth-token: <token>` (bearer plugin behaviour, dist/plugins/bearer/index.mjs:64-65, harmless and lets a Better Auth client pick the token), 200 {redirect:false, token, url: undefined (omit the key), user}.
- GET /api/auth/get-session: actor via 4.1 restricted to via 'jwt' (an insta_ key → `null`); null → `reply.send(null)` with content-type application/json (body `null`, status 200, session.mjs:43); else 200 {session: sessionOut(row, token), user: betterAuthUser(admin)}. token in sessionOut is the plaintext presented by the caller (the row stores only the hash), which is what the cloud reads back at service.ts:72-77.
- POST /api/auth/sign-out: resolve via cookie first then bearer; if found revokeSession; always clear the cookie; 200 {success:true}.
- POST /auth/login: {email,password} → same checks as sign-in (shared function) but errors map to the cloud wrapper shape: 400 {error:'invalid email'} / 401 {error:'unauthorized'} / 429 {error:'too many attempts'}; success → mintSession, NO cookie (the cloud wrapper returns tokens only; the console stores them itself, insta-frontend src/lib/api/session.ts:31-42), 200 {accessToken: token, refreshToken: token, expiresIn: floor((expiresAt - now)/1000), user: PublicUser}.
- POST /auth/refresh: {refreshToken}; findSession (bearer semantics, insta_ keys rejected) → 200 AuthResult with the SAME token (no rotation, service.ts:200-204) else 401 {error:'unauthorized'}.
- POST /auth/logout: body.refreshToken → revokeSession if it resolves; always 200 {ok:true}.
- POST /auth/signup → 501 notCloud text pointing at `${consoleUrl}/setup`.
- GET /me: actor from the guard; admin → 200 {user: publicUser(admin), via}. publicUser = {id, email, name, avatarUrl: null, emailVerified: true}.
- GET /tokens, POST /tokens, DELETE /tokens/:tokenId: section 3.4, shapes per routes table. POST validates body.orgId: undefined|null accepted, anything else 400.
- betterAuthUser(admin) = {id, name, email, emailVerified: true, image: null, createdAt, updatedAt}. sessionOut(row, token) = {id, token, userId, expiresAt, createdAt, updatedAt, ipAddress, userAgent}. apiTokenOut(row) = row minus keyHash.
Local mode: registerAuth registers exactly today's `/me` → {user: LOCAL_USER} and the three /tokens 501s with today's text (server.ts:55,58-60); nothing else, no hook.

## 8. state.json discipline
### 8.1 Why not a mutex
mutate() is synchronous (state.ts:32-37): readFileSync → fn → writeFileSync with no await, so two mutate() calls can never interleave inside one Node process; the only real hazards are (a) a crash mid-write leaving a truncated file, (b) somebody adding an await inside fn, (c) a second daemon process on the same file, (d) write amplification from high-frequency fields. The spec's 'write lock (the router stamps from many requests)' is met by (d): stamps never touch state.json.
### 8.2 Atomic write
saveState: tmp = `${p}.tmp-${process.pid}-${++seq}`; writeFileSync(tmp, json); renameSync(tmp, p). rename is atomic on POSIX for same-filesystem paths; the tmp lives next to the target. No fsync (a power loss can lose the last write but never corrupts the file; documented).
### 8.3 Sync-only assertion
mutate: `const out = fn(s); if (out && typeof (out as {then?: unknown}).then === 'function') throw new Error('mutate() callbacks must be synchronous: read state, decide, write; await outside')`. Existing callers all return plain values (checked: engine.ts, govern.ts).
### 8.4 Parse cache
loadState: statSync(p) → {mtimeMs, size}; if equal to the cached key return structuredClone(cached); else parse and cache. Correct because this process is the only writer (8.5) and every write goes through saveState which updates the cache immediately after rename. Saves one JSON.parse per request now that the guard reads state on every call.
### 8.5 Heartbeat lock file
acquireLock(dataDir): p = join(dataDir,'instad.lock'); payload = JSON.stringify({pid, bootId: randomUUID(), startedAt: iso, host: os.hostname()}).
1. try openSync(p, 'wx') → write payload → held.
2. on EEXIST: st = statSync(p); if now - st.mtimeMs > 60_000 → stale (the previous holder stopped heartbeating; covers a killed container whose pid namespace makes process.kill(pid,0) meaningless) → unlinkSync then retry step 1 once; else read the payload and throw Error(`another instad (pid ${pid}, started ${startedAt}) holds ${dataDir}; stop it or point INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR elsewhere`).
3. heartbeat: setInterval(() => utimesSync(p, now, now), 20_000).unref().
releaseLock(): clearInterval; flush touchLater buffer; unlinkSync(p) only if the file still carries our bootId. Called from the SIGTERM/SIGINT handler and `process.on('exit')`.
### 8.6 Coalesced touches
touchLater(fn): push fn to a buffer; start (once) an unref'd 30 s interval that runs `mutate(s => { for (const f of buffer) f(s); buffer.length = 0 })`; releaseLock flushes synchronously. Used for token.lastUsedAt, session.updatedAt/expiresAt slide, expired-session deletion. Everything else keeps using mutate() directly. Note for the reconciler: fns must be idempotent and must tolerate the row having been deleted meanwhile (look the row up by id inside fn, no captured references).
### 8.7 What must stay out of state.json
Activity stamps (router/scheduler), in-flight op markers, RSS samples, rate-limiter buckets, wake singleflight maps: all in-memory. On restart the scheduler treats boot time as every service's stamp (its own createGrace analogue), which is why persistence is unnecessary.

## 9. `instad --reset-admin`
loadConfig; refuse in local mode ('nothing to reset in local mode'); initStatePath; mutate: if !identity?.admin → print 'no admin exists' and exit 0; else identity.previousAdminId = admin.id; admin = null; sessions = []; tokens untouched. Print `admin removed; open ${consoleUrl}/setup to create a new one (existing insta_ tokens keep working once it exists)`. Runs without the lock (it is a one-shot process); if a daemon is running it sees the new state on its next loadState (cache keyed on mtime) and the guard rejects the dead admin immediately (4.1c).

## 10. Compatibility matrix after this WP
- `insta status` (GET /me): local unchanged; server needs a token/session.
- `insta login --api-key K --api-url https://api.<d>`: GET /me with Bearer K → {user} (auth.ts:98-111) ✅.
- `insta login --email e --api-url …`: POST /auth/login → AuthResult ✅; later 401s retry /auth/refresh with the same token ✅; `insta logout` → /auth/logout ✅.
- `insta login` bare / `--device` / `--oauth`: POST /api/auth/device/code → 404 JSON from the not-found handler (no Better Auth device plugin here). Acceptable: the CLI prints the daemon's error; documented as unsupported (no mailer, no OAuth) in COMPATIBILITY.md.
- MCP with a static bearer (`insta setup --mcp-token`, setup.ts:225-233 POSTs /tokens with an existing session) ✅ in server mode.
- Console (insta-frontend) is NOT served by the daemon; it is not a client of this design.

Docker (integrator only, sequential): none required by WP1. Optional smoke in the packaging WP: boot `INSTA_OSS_MODE=server INSTA_OSS_DOMAIN=x.test INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR=$tmp npx tsx src/main.ts`, curl /healthz 200, curl /me 401, POST sign-up, curl /me with the cookie 200, second daemon on the same data dir exits non-zero with the lock message.
UI: `cd ui && npm run build` typechecks the new pages; no browser test in this WP (no e2e harness exists yet; the public e2e in M6 adds 'setup page and token login').
risks: Origin split in server mode: the dashboard is served on console.<domain> and calls relative paths, so the API must also be reachable on console.<domain> (the router forwards both hosts to the same listener); if the router WP forwards only api.<domain>, the SPA breaks. Stated as engine seam (2) and (1).

Cookie name parity: `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` requires https; when an operator runs server mode with INSTA_OSS_CONSOLE_URL=http://… (no edge yet) the cookie drops the prefix and Secure, which is intended, but a later switch to https invalidates existing browser sessions (users sign in again).

Brute force: sign-in is public on a VPS; the in-memory limiter is per process and per IP; behind the edge, req.ip depends on trustProxy and a correct X-Forwarded-For (the edge is ours, so acceptable; if the ask/edge is misconfigured all attempts share one IP and the limiter is too strict rather than too loose).
Single admin means a lost password is recovered only via `--reset-admin` on the box; documented, no email flow.

shell injection replaces the static index.html serving path; a Vite build that ever inlines `</head>` differently would make the replace a no-op and the SPA would fall back to 'local' assumptions in server mode (guard: server-auth test 9 asserts the marker is present).

Stale-lock takeover at 60 s of missed heartbeats could in theory evict a live daemon frozen for a minute (e.g. a stop-the-world host); the evicted process keeps running until it next writes, and its writes go through rename so the file stays intact, but two writers could alternate for a while. Accepted for v1; the installer never starts two.
Scopes accepted but not enforced: a token minted with `scopes: ['read']` has full power on the daemon. Documented; the cloud enforces scopes at the org role layer we do not have.
Local mode now imports config.ts and identity.ts; any accidental behaviour change is caught by test/server.test.ts, which must pass unchanged.
